comments.text: Installs the road table pointers $2591 and $26D1, patches the colour source $27C1 and sets the script and scenery table pointers to $15CB and $16A3.
The 81 little-endian dispatch and operand words for round 4. $7A1F jumps through the word indexed by twice $12. The opening $7A33 takes the next word, $1681, as the initial scenery stream pointer.
Round 4 scenery descriptor pointer table with 16 entries. Indices 0–8 point into the engine. Indices 9–15 point into this stage. $8EBC reads a pointer after scaling the object type by two.

Eight forty-byte rows of glyph values. $8C86 uses this base when selecting the alternate height band and advances the source by 80 bytes per displayed row. The glyph values index the colour table at $27C1.
First four raw rows from the second band source patched into $8D34/$8D35. $8C0E selects a clipped phase and $8CF9 turns the glyph values into both screen and colour bytes.
Round 4 maps each road glyph index to its colour RAM value here. The stage prologue patches this base into $8D03/$8D04 and $9109/$910A for the road-band and scenery blitters.
Toggles $A7D0 and advances the road script. Exchanges the glyph colour and both road-band pointer pairs with the three stored alternatives, then swaps 1,584 glyph bytes with VIC RAM from $F9C8.
Three addresses saved by the exchange. They are the glyph colour lookup and the two road band tables for the active surface after the next swap.
Road surface glyph bytes exchanged with $F9C8–$FDC7. After the exchange this region keeps the glyph bytes of the alternate surface for the next call.
Road surface glyph bytes exchanged with $FDC8–$FFF7. After the exchange this region keeps the glyph bytes of the alternate surface for the next call.
Alternate sprite bank 1, shape indices $00–$0F. Index 1 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $C000–$C3FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 1, shape indices $10–$1F. Index 1 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $C400–$C7FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Continues the first alternate lower sprite bank, from shape index $14 through $1F. This subrange is exchanged with $C500–$C7FF by $9B76.

The round 4 load writes one byte here in the inherited music image. Other bytes in the music image carry over from its preceding round.
Sixteen 64-byte sprite slots with shape indices $00–$0F in VIC bank $C000. Each shape starts with 21 rows of three bytes and leaves the 64th byte outside the displayed shape.
Second byte of sprite slot zero in the currently installed low sprite set. The displayed shape includes this byte and the asset selector can test it before exchanging sets.
Sixteen shape slots $10–$1F in the loaded sprite set. The bank-relative pointer is the slot number and the VIC multiplies it by 64.
Shape slots $20–$2F use RAM $C800–$CBFF. The stage’s object placement code passes shape indices to the raster sprite allocator.
Four final shape slots in the stage’s low-bank sprite block, from $30 at $CC00 to $33 at $CCC0.
Sprite area for VIC indices $88–$97, sixteen 64-byte slots. The raster multiplexer writes the shape indices of scheduled objects to both pointer tables.
Shape slots $98–$A7 continue the second stage sprite block. Slots $A0–$A7 also occupy the first half of the character memory selected by the dashboard split.
Eight sprite slots $A8–$AF in the last two pages of the replacement upper sprite block.
Stage 4 replaces the road character set starting at glyph $39. This segment reaches the penultimate complete glyph slot and the opening byte of slot $FF.
Upper half of the road character set. Groups of eight bytes give the timed road display its cell rows. The load’s final byte is at $FFF8 and the CPU uses the final hardware vector bytes separately.
